mentl/17c5348:
The banked separating probe ran first and killed the name it was banked
under. One program holding both a closed and an open record with the same
known fields answers closed-correct and open-wrong side by side; a shared
generated helper would have forced one answer for both. So fold_sig's
TRecord/TRecordOpen collapse is not the mechanism — the eq leaf walks the
known field list.

That pointed at the root, which is worse than the eq face. An open row's
field offsets come from the known set's own ordering rather than the
runtime record's. `fn pick(u: {zeta: Int, ...}) = u.zeta` over
{alpha: 7, zeta: 9} returns 7: zeta is the only known field, so it takes
index 0, which the real record uses for alpha. Silent — no diagnostic, no
trap, check passes. The closed twin returns 9.

It is SYNTAX's own example. The row-polymorphism section offers
`fn greet(u: {name: String, ...}) = "Hello, " ++ u.name` as the feature's
worked form, and that exact shape measured as `fn width(u: {name: Int,
...}) = u.name + 1` over {name: 5, age: 9} returns 10, which is age + 1.

One rule, four consumers: the pattern takes offsets from the pattern's own
index, == walks the known field list, field access takes the known set's
index, and LFieldLoad floors loudly only where offset resolution returns
-1 — which is why the inferred-open case traps while the annotated-open
case silently misreads. That split is measured, not explained; tracing
which branch each site takes is the next probe.

No src change, and the blocker is structural: the offsets must be
resolved, since the march already refuted the blanket floor, and
resolving requires the receiver's real layout to reach the consumer.

Lands tests/syntax/record-field-param-closed with contract 9, the control
that made the finding precise, battery at five. SYNTAX now records the
measured gap beneath its example, because a reader would otherwise trust
it; SYNTAX stays the authority and the lathe has not been turned to it.

The module dep walk ran a full lex + parse_program on every module,

mentl/17b8432:
reachable_from_main computed the emitted-fn set by calling reach_decl_refs
per frontier name -- a linear scan of the whole lowered decl list (via
last/drop_last per name), O(N^2), perf-pinned at 58.66% of the 56s
self-compile. Replace it with build_reach_index (one pass, name -> refs) +
reach_index_get (O(1) str_hash bucket lookup); reach_grow / reach_enqueue /
reach_has / rbuf / fbuf are unchanged.

The index alone HUNG m2 (m3-gen over a 500s guard). An adversarial diagnosis
-- a 5-agent workflow reading the code plus an independent binary-patch
ground-truth probe on the built m2, both converging -- found a PRE-EXISTING
latent bug the index exposed, not an index defect: reach_names_expr's
LSuspend arm prepended LSuspend's second field as a reachable name, but that
field is op_h, an Int op-handle (LSuspend(Int, Int, LowExpr, [LowExpr], List,
Bool)). The raw Int was enqueued and, at reach_grow iteration 270, looked up:
reach_decl_refs compared it with str_eq, whose length short-circuit rejects
it O(1) without reading its bytes, so the scan tolerated it; reach_index_get
calls str_hash, which has no short-circuit and reads all byte_len(name)
bytes. The Int read as a string pointer (op_h = 72051) lands in the static
data section at the WAT-template text " (local $nc ", whose first four bytes
" (lo" = 0x6f6c2820 are misread as a flat-string length of 1,869,359,136
(~1.87 GB); str_hash then grinds ~1.87 billion bytes -- the hang.

Drop the [o] prepend (op_h is an Int, the callee is already reached via the
fn_expr f; op_h is a dispatch index, never a fn name). This killed the hang
AND made reach more precise: boot's garbage-tolerant scan spuriously kept
$println (dead in the compiler binary -- its only callers are test.mn's
main-unreachable harness), which the leaner reach correctly drops. So m2 !=
m3 by one fn plus its shifted indices -- a TRANSITION, not a defect.
